content.title: FAA Announces First US Digital Air Traffic Control Towers
content.caption: The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) has announced the first digital air traffic control towers in the US, bringing new technology to smaller airports in Florida and Alaska.

slides.heading: FAA Announces Digital Air Traffic Control Towers
slides.text: The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) announces the first digital air traffic control towers in the US, bringing new technology to smaller airports in Florida and Alaska.
slides.image_search_query: FAA digital air traffic control towers United States

slides.heading: Technology and Air Traffic Control
slides.text: The FAA's new digital air traffic control towers use advanced camera systems and digital displays to provide controllers with a continuous, 360-degree view of airport operations.
slides.image_search_query: advanced camera systems, digital displays United States

slides.heading: Impact on Air Traffic
slides.text: The FAA maintains that the technology is not intended to replace human controllers, but rather to provide greater visibility and additional information to help controllers perform their existing duties.
slides.image_search_query: human controllers, greater visibility United States

slides.heading: Concerns and Challenges
slides.text: The implementation of new technology in air traffic control has raised concerns about the types of technology being used and the potential impact on air safety.
